description: Convert any annual salary to hourly, daily, weekly, and monthly pay instantly. Includes a reference table for common salaries ($30k–$200k) and the exact formula used by the U.S. OPM.
answerSnippet: To convert annual salary to hourly: divide the salary by total work hours per year (hours/week × weeks/year). The U.S. standard is 2,080 hours (40 hrs × 52 weeks). Quick reference: $50,000/yr = $24.04/hr; $75,000/yr = $36.06/hr; $100,000/yr = $48.08/hr; $150,000/yr = $72.12/hr — all gross (pre-tax) at a standard 40-hr week.

explanation:
## Annual Salary to Hourly Rate: Formula

The conversion divides your annual salary by total work hours in the year:

```
Total Hours/Year = Hours per Week × Weeks per Year
Hourly Rate     = Annual Salary ÷ Total Hours/Year
Daily Rate      = Hourly Rate × 8
Weekly Pay      = Hourly Rate × Hours per Week
Biweekly Pay    = Weekly Pay × 2
Monthly Pay     = Annual Salary ÷ 12
```

The **U.S. standard full-time work year** is **2,080 hours** (40 hrs/week × 52 weeks), the figure used by the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) for federal civilian pay rates.

## Annual Salary to Hourly Rate — Reference Table

All figures assume **40 hrs/week × 52 weeks = 2,080 hours/year**, gross (pre-tax).

## Worked Example

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| Annual Salary | $75,000 |
| Hours per Week | 40 |
| Weeks per Year | 52 |

| Output | Calculation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Total Hours | 40 × 52 | 2,080 hrs |
| Hourly Rate | $75,000 ÷ 2,080 | **$36.06/hr** |
| Daily Rate | $36.06 × 8 | **$288.46/day** |
| Weekly Pay | $36.06 × 40 | **$1,442.31/wk** |
| Biweekly Pay | $1,442.31 × 2 | **$2,884.62** |
| Monthly Pay | $75,000 ÷ 12 | **$6,250.00/mo** |

## Adjusting for Real-World Schedules

- **Part-time or seasonal work:** Reduce weeks per year (e.g., 48 weeks if you take 4 weeks unpaid leave). This raises your effective hourly cost to an employer.
- **Overtime-heavy roles:** If you regularly work 50 hrs/week, set hours to 50. Your true hourly equivalent drops — a $75,000 salary at 50 hrs/week = $28.85/hr, not $36.06.
- **Freelance rate buffer:** Freelancers should target 25–35% above their equivalent salaried hourly rate to cover self-employment taxes (~15.3%), benefits, and unpaid downtime.

## Gross vs. Net Pay

All results are **before taxes**. Federal income tax, state income tax, and FICA (Social Security + Medicare, 7.65% employee share) reduce your actual take-home. Use a dedicated paycheck calculator for after-tax estimates.

faq.q: How do I convert annual salary to hourly rate?
faq.a: Divide your annual salary by total work hours per year. For a standard 40-hr week and 52 weeks: Annual Salary ÷ 2,080 = Hourly Rate. Example: $75,000 ÷ 2,080 = $36.06/hr gross.
$50,000 per year equals $24.04 per hour at a standard 40-hour week (2,080 hours/year). Daily: $192.31. Weekly: $961.54. Monthly: $4,166.67 — all pre-tax.
$100,000 per year equals $48.08 per hour on a standard 40-hr, 52-week schedule. Daily: $384.62. Weekly: $1,923.08. Monthly: $8,333.33 — all gross (pre-tax).

faq.q: What is the standard number of work hours in a year?
faq.a: The U.S. standard is 2,080 hours per year, based on 40 hours per week × 52 weeks. The U.S. Office of Personnel Management uses this figure for federal civilian pay rates. Some employers use 2,087 hours for more precise calculations.

faq.q: Should I include vacation weeks when calculating my hourly rate?
faq.a: If your employer pays you during vacation (PTO), keep weeks at 52 — you're paid for those weeks even without working. If your time off is unpaid, subtract those weeks. For example, 2 weeks unpaid = 50 weeks, which raises your hourly rate since the same salary covers fewer hours.

faq.q: How do I use this to set my freelance rate?
faq.a: Find your equivalent salaried hourly rate, then add 25–40% to cover self-employment tax (15.3%), health insurance, retirement contributions, and unbillable hours. A $36.06 salaried equivalent should translate to at least $45–$50/hr as a freelancer to break even.

faq.q: Does this calculator account for taxes?
faq.a: No. All outputs are gross (pre-tax) figures. After federal income tax, state tax, and FICA (Social Security + Medicare, 7.65% employee share), your net take-home will be meaningfully lower. Use a dedicated paycheck calculator for after-tax estimates.

faq.q: What's the difference between biweekly and semimonthly pay?
faq.a: Biweekly means 26 paychecks per year (every 2 weeks). Semimonthly means 24 paychecks per year (twice per month). This calculator shows biweekly pay (weekly × 2). Semimonthly pay = annual salary ÷ 24.

faq.q: Is monthly pay calculated as annual ÷ 12 or weekly × 4?
faq.a: This calculator uses annual salary ÷ 12, which is the standard payroll method. Multiplying weekly pay by 4 gives only 48 weeks of pay per year and underestimates monthly income by about 8.3%.

faq.q: What if I work 50 hours a week? How does that change my hourly rate?
faq.a: Working 50 hrs/week instead of 40 with the same salary lowers your effective hourly rate. Example: $75,000 ÷ (50 × 52) = $75,000 ÷ 2,600 = $28.85/hr — about 20% less than the standard 40-hr rate of $36.06/hr.

referenceTables.caption: The other direction: what a given hourly rate works out to per year, week and month at a standard full-time schedule (40 hrs/week × 52 weeks = 2,080 hrs/year). Gross, pre-tax. Useful for freelancers and contractors quoting an hourly rate against a target annual income.
referenceTables.note: Annual = hourly × 2,080. A common freelance rule of thumb: divide your target annual salary by 1,000 for a rough billable hourly rate (e.g. $100k target ≈ $100/hr) — that ~2× markup over the literal $48/hr at 2,080 hours covers self-employment tax, benefits and unbillable time.
